verdict: Welltower grew revenue 38% to $3.72B as a wave of seniors-housing acquisitions landed, and normalized FFO per share jumped 25% to $1.67 on 21% same-store profit growth in its housing portfolio.

segments.name: Resident fees and services
segments.note: What residents pay for housing, care and services in the seniors-housing communities Welltower operates — up 51% as acquired portfolios joined and occupancy and room rates rose.

segments.name: Rental income
segments.note: Rent from tenants who lease Welltower's properties — outpatient medical, skilled nursing and triple-net seniors housing — down 2% as some leased properties were sold or converted.

segments.name: Interest and other income
segments.note: Interest on loans Welltower has made ($83M) plus other income ($23M) — other income fell because a year ago it included larger one-off items.

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of buildings and other assets over their useful lives — a large, non-cash REIT cost.

opex.name: Other expenses
opex.note: Other property and corporate costs as printed, up sharply with the enlarged portfolio.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Head-office running costs — finance, legal and management.

opex.name: Impairment of assets
opex.note: Writing down properties worth less than their book value.

opex.name: Debt extinguishment and loan provisions
opex.note: A $7M loss on paying off debt early, plus a small provision for loan losses.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $193M and a $31M loss from unconsolidated entities, partly offset by a $115M gain on real estate sales — a net $109M cost below operating income.
oneTimers: A $115M gain on real estate dispositions and acquisitions of controlling interests lifted net income (versus a $4M gain a year ago).
Impairment charges of $33M and a $7M loss on extinguishment of debt also sit in this quarter's expenses.

takeaways.title: Acquisitions transformed the top line
takeaways.text: Revenue jumped to $3.72B as resident fees rose 51%. Welltower completed $13.3B of investments in the first nine months and had $21.0B closed or under contract for the year.

takeaways.title: Seniors housing is booming
takeaways.text: Same-store NOI in the seniors housing operating portfolio grew 21.0%, on 320 basis points of occupancy growth and 5.3% growth in revenue per occupied room; total portfolio same-store NOI grew 15.8%.

takeaways.title: Cash earnings per share leapt
takeaways.text: Normalized FFO — the cash-earnings yardstick for REITs — rose 24.6% per share to $1.67, and Welltower raised full-year guidance to $6.47–$6.53. Net debt was just 3.02x adjusted EBITDA.

footerNote: Welltower is a real estate investment trust (REIT). Figures are converted from the 10-Q's thousands and rounded to $M. Interest expense is shown in Other income (together with the gain on property sales and losses from unconsolidated entities) rather than in operating expenses. Net income of $415M is consolidated; $397M ($0.54 per diluted share) was attributable to common stockholders after $18M for noncontrolling interests. FFO and normalized FFO are non-GAAP REIT measures reconciled in the release; GAAP net income is the bottom line used here.
